title.narrative: Improved skills and decent employment for youth and vulnerable groups

description.narrative:
The strategy advances a job-rich economic recovery and sustainable development through an integrated and multifaceted approach. It prioritizes investments in skills development and skills alignment to better respond to evolving labour market needs and to address persistent skills mismatches that constrain productivity and limit the effective harnessing of the demographic dividend. These efforts will be complemented by targeted support to the private sector to stimulate productive employment creation, enterprise development, and improved labour market outcomes, particularly for youth and women.
The strategy further seeks to strengthen governance and institutional capacity in skills and employment systems, promoting more inclusive, equitable, and responsive policies and delivery mechanisms. Specific attention will be given to expanding access to quality skills development and employment opportunities for vulnerable and under-represented groups, reinforcing the ILO’s commitment to inclusion and leaving no one behind.
Decent work is placed at the centre of crisis response and recovery efforts, with a strong focus on Employment-Intensive Investment Programmes (EIIPs). These programmes will support immediate job creation and income generation while contributing to longer-term development objectives, including local economic development, social cohesion, and resilience to economic and climate-related shocks.
During the biennium, the strategy will emphasize integrated policy approaches and sustainable financing through support to the Global Accelerator for Jobs and Social Protection for Just Transitions. In addition, constituents will be supported to assess the employment and decent work implications of digitalization, including digital labour platforms. This will strengthen evidence-based policy dialogue on platform work while exploring the use of digital solutions to enhance service delivery.
